text:
IncidentBot: PAGE: oncall (us-west-2) — GPU pool saturation detected for spot-gpu pool. Auto-remediation attempted. Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/bridge/abc123

Alice SRE: seeing queue growth across the inference-queue; dashboard spike at 10:12 UTC. Requests piling into the fs-queue, latency > 2s.

Josh Eng: confirmed — autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts then a hard reject: `scale_up suppressed: cloud_quota_limit` and `allocation_error: insufficient fallback capacity`.

Alice SRE: snippet from autoscaler logs:
```
[10:11:54] scale_decision: desired=120 current=40 pending=78
[10:11:55] request_scale_up -> api->cloud: create_instances(80)
[10:11:56] cloud: quota_exceeded (GPUs)
[10:11:56] fallback: attempt_to_route_to_reserved=false -> error: no compatible reserved pools found
[10:11:56] result: scale_failed_quota
```

Ben Platform: our spot pool just had a preemptible wave earlier; many nodes drained. Reserved pools are near their soft-cap because of a scheduled batch job in eu-west. We're not bleeding capacity across regions automatically.

Maria Oncall: what's current queue length?

Alice SRE: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l queue=production` shows ~140 Pending, ~36 Running. Pod events: `Insufficient gpu` repeated.

Support: customers reporting elevated 5xx for inference endpoints; severity-high for a handful of paying customers on standard tier. No dedicated customers broken yet but degraded. CS has opened tickets.

Josh Eng: quick mitigation options — list from runbook: 1) throttle ingest (rate-limit new requests), 2) enable fallback model variant (lower memory/quantized) for non-SLA routes, 3) borrow capacity from reserved pool in us-east, 4) kill large non-critical batch jobs. Which can we do quickly?

Ben Platform: we can toggle cross-region routing but it takes ~7–10m for traffic shifts and we need to ensure latency SLO for callers. Reserved pool in us-east has spare nodes (20 GPUs) but models there are slightly older. We can also temporarily scale down off-peak batch job `data-hopper` (it uses 24 GPUs).

Alice SRE: I'm going to invoke throttles on internal ingestion and enable the fallback routing policy for non-privileged keys. Pushing config change now.

Alice SRE: applying rate-limit config:
```bash
rbctl routes update --route inference-ingest --qps 1000 --burst 200
rbctl policies set --name fallback_non_sla --variant small-ggml-8bit
```

DeployBot: config-change accepted: routes.update (id=r12345) by Alice SRE.

Alice SRE: also sent `kubectl scale deployment data-hopper -n batch --replicas=0` to drain the 24 GPUs allocated to batch.

DeployBot: deployment scaled (data-hopper) — 24 GPUs freed.

Josh Eng: good, freeing batch helps. Now requesting cross-region borrow from us-east reserved: Ben, can you open the cross-region routing toggle?

Ben Platform: doing it. Patching routing policy to allow us-east fallback and marking model-compatibility flag. This will accept slightly older model with `max_seq_len=1024`.

Ben Platform: patch applied. Now creating 20 spot-like reservations in us-east and triggering node provisioning.

Alice SRE: autoscaler is retrying. New log lines show partial progress: `provisioned 18/20`, but there's an error: `node_registration_timeout` for 2 nodes.

Josh Eng: if two nodes fail to join, we still have ~38 GPUs freed from batch + 18 provisioned = 56. Desired was 80, so still short. We need additional mitigations: (A) broaden fallback to quantized-4bit variant for low-priority traffic, (B) enable model-splitting to route big calls to smaller sequences, (C) temporarily increase token-cost per call to slow down abuse.

Support: will inform impacted customers: status page blurb drafted — "We are experiencing increased latency and errors for some inference requests in us-west-2 due to GPU capacity constraints; mitigations in progress."

Alice SRE: executing broader fallback now: update policy to allow quantized-4bit for route /generate for non-enterprise keys.

Alice SRE: applying:
```yaml
policies:
  - route: /generate
    condition: key_tier != enterprise
    action: use_model_variant: gptx-small-4bit
```

DeployBot: policy applied (id=p5566).

Maria Oncall: I'm starting the incident timeline for handoff. Current customer impact: 18 customers with >1% error rate, 3 customers flagged as high-impact due to latency spikes. Escalation to product done.

Josh Eng: queue length trending down slowly. Pending pods fell from 140 -> 72 in 18 minutes. Latency still high for large sequences.

Alice SRE: note — autoscaler still logs occasional `suppress_scale: preemption_pressure` which indicates cloud-side preemption events interfering with steady scaling. We should mark blocked zones as 'no-schedule' for new spot allocations for next 30m to avoid repeated churn.

Ben Platform: marking problematic AZs in us-west-2 as no-schedule. This should stabilize scheduling decisions.

Alice SRE: also discovered a config bug in the fallback selection logic: reserved_pool_compatibility was only checking GPU memory, not kernel version. That's why some us-east nodes were rejected earlier. I'll patch that check.

Josh Eng: patch ready, rolling now.

Alice SRE: patch rolled. Autoscaler now recognizes us-east nodes as compatible. Provisioning completes — additional 18 nodes registered. Pending now down to 16.

Support: status page updated and customers notified. Tickets triaged, CS monitoring.

Maria Oncall: handing off to night oncall in 30 minutes. Will produce a short handoff note with what changed and recommended watch metrics.

Maria Oncall: handoff note (to paste):
- Incident start: 2024-04-10T10:11:xxZ
- Symptom: large queue growth and 5xx spike due to spot preemption + quota hits
- Actions taken: throttled ingestion, scaled down batch (data-hopper), enabled quantized fallback, borrowed reserved capacity us-east, marked AZs no-schedule, patched fallback compatibility check.
- Current state: queue draining, pending pods ~16, latency improving, customers still under watch.
- Next steps: monitor pending pod count, request new node registrations, consider temporary SLA credits for high-impacted customers if regression persists.

Alice SRE: leaving log pointers and runbook links:
Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/gpu-pool-saturation
Autoscaler logs: https://logs.redwood/streams/auto-1732109876

Josh Eng: can we add a short-term metric alert to catch re-churn? Suggest alert if pending_pods > 50 for 5m or scale_errors > 3 in 2m.

Ben Platform: alert added.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, impact reduced. Will remain open for monitoring.

Alice SRE: handing off active pager to Maria Oncall now. Leaving Slack thread for continuity.

Maria Oncall: I acknowledge. I'll take the remainder and escalate to infra if we see a new preemption wave.

Support: closing loop with customers: we're offering a 10% credit to the three most-impacted customers; CS to coordinate refunds.

Maria Oncall: last check at 10:58 UTC: pending pods 8, request latency back to baseline for enterprise customers, non-enterprise still behind on some routes but falling. Marking incident as monitoring.

Alice SRE: thanks team. I'll follow up tomorrow with a post-incident summary and an action item to increase cross-region reserved buffer for peak windows.

Josh Eng: +1 on postmortem. Also propose we add a quick synthetic test for fallback compatibility on node registration to catch kernel mismatches early.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED -> monitoring mode.
